messages:
Evelyn: Quick sync — I'm proposing we split the admit probe into two explicit responsibilities: sampling (what inputs we pick) and orchestration (how we schedule/run benches). Thoughts on tradeoffs?

Ajay: +1 to separation. Sampling is really policy-heavy and will change more often. Orchestration should remain stable and focus on reliability/backpressure.

Leah: Agree. One concern: if sampling is too aggressive we bias the bench and hide regressions. Need to encode stratification guarantees.

Tom: Can we have a thin contract between them: sampler returns a BatchDescriptor and orchestration implements run(BatchDescriptor) -> ResultBundle? keeps interfaces small.

Evelyn: Exactly. Proposed minimal contract: sampler -> list of sample ids + metadata (seqlen, weight, golden_flag). orchestration uses metadata to pick execution path (fastpath vs deepbench).

Ravi: How do we handle golden vs stochastic samples? Should orchestration treat golden samples with stronger invariants (no caching, fixed seeds)?

Ajay: Yes — orchestration should accept execution hints. Example hint set: {force_fresh_kv: true, seed: 1234, timeout_ms: 45000}. Orchestration doesn't implement sampling logic, just obeys hints.

Leah: We should also surface sample provenance. If something regresses we want to re-run exact sample. So sampler must return stable identifiers and a reproducible payload.

Tom: Implementation sketch: sampler service exposes endpoints: /sample?policy=golden&size=64 and /snapshot?id=...; response includes payload_uri and fingerprint. orchestration pulls payload and runs.

Evelyn: Pseudo-config for orchestration:
```
orchestrator:
  concurrency: 8
  max_retries: 2
  hint_timeout_ms: 500
  shard_mode: seqlen-aware
```

Ravi: What about latency SLOs for the bench run? Some benches are long (deep eval). We need a tiering mechanism so we don't starve quick smoke runs.

Ajay: Use priority queues in orchestrator. Samples come with priority label from sampler (smoke, full, golden). Orchestration enforces capacity per tier.

Leah: Observability: sampler should emit selection_weights and feature-distribution metrics. Orchestrator emits queue depth, run duration, failure reasons, GPU-utilization tag. Link them in console by batch_id.

Tom: Failure handling: if a run fails with OOM, orchestrator should attempt fallback to quantized variant or route to slowpath offline bench and mark sample flaky. Sampler should be able to mark model as 'needs-profile' so we get a targeted profiling sweep.

Evelyn: Important tradeoff: centralizing sampling gives better global coverage but is a single change risk. Decentralized local samplers are more resilient but may diverge. Which direction?

Ajay: I'd prefer central policy + local cached samplers. Central controller decides policies and rolls them out; local samplers maintain cache and can continue if controller is unreachable.

Ravi: Can we leverage existing KV caching service for payloads? sampler returns payload_uri pointing to KV or objectstore. If orchestrator can't fetch payload we mark sample transient-failure and requeue.

Leah: One more: privacy/regulatory models. For private deployments we can't upload payloads to central store. Sampler must support local-only mode where payloads never leave customer VPC. Orchestrator must run in same VPC.

Evelyn: Good callout. Design note: add a "deployment_mode" field on BatchDescriptor: hosted | dedicated | private. Orchestrator picks storage/exec path accordingly.

Tom: Minimal API example for BatchDescriptor:
```
{
  id: sample-20260301-0001,
  payload_uri: s3://bench-payloads/2026/03/01/0001.json,
  features: { seqlen: 128, tokens: 42 },
  hints: { priority: smoke, timeout_ms: 20000, force_fresh_kv: false },
  provenance: { sampler_version: v2.3, policy_id: strat-2026-03 }
}
```

Ajay: Matches what I had in mind. We should add a fingerprint field for reproducibility.

Leah: Operational concern: rolling sampler policy changes need a canary. Suggest policy rollout with shadow sampling for a window before making it authoritative.

Ravi: benchbot: when sampler policy rolls out, emit diff-summary of selection distributions to central telemetry. benchbot: noted.

benchbot: policy-rollout detected. sampler:v2.3 -> v2.4. sample-distribution-delta: {short: +4.2%, long: -3.1%}.

Evelyn: Next steps: draft RFC with API contracts, sample lifecycle, and failure modes. I'll sketch the interfaces and a small PoC for orchestrator priority queues. Anyone want to volunteer to own the sampler PoC?

Leah: I'll pick up sampler PoC. Will start with central policy + local cache approach.

Ajay: I'll prototype orchestrator queueing and hint handling.

Evelyn: Great — thanks all. I'll create RFC and link this thread.
